Summary

The entry file declares 7 imports — 5 external (context, errors, fmt, strings std-lib, plus github.com/google/uuid, github.com/jackc/pgx/v5, github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool third-party) and 2 project-local (internal/notifications/rules and internal/webhooks). The file sits at the service layer of the artefactitems package (per <pkg>/service.go convention) and holds two pools: vectorArtefactsPool (vaPool — vector_artefacts DB) and mainPool (mmff_vector for owner decoration only). 0 violations. 1 informational warning: the service holds two pools, which is documented and intentional (vaPool primary, mainPool read-only) but worth flagging against the “one pool per service” convention. Headline verdict: clean — direction is correct, no transport-DTO leak, no handler import, cross-package coupling is through an inverted interface (TopologyScopeResolver) which is the documented pattern.

Entry file layer

backend/internal/artefactitems/service.go — service layer for the artefactitems package. Per .claude/CLAUDE.md and the package’s own sql.go header comment (PLA-0048 / RF1.2.19), this file is the sole writer for artefacts and artefacts_fields_values in vector_artefacts, plus read-only against mmff_vector for owner decoration and workspace resolution. Rules that apply (from docs/c_c_db_routing.md + docs/c_c_transport_segregation.md):

  • Direction: handler → service → sql. Service may import other services (here: only via interface to avoid cycles).
  • Must NOT import handlers, transport DTO packages, or frontend code.
  • Pool ownership: by spec, ONE pool. This service intentionally holds two (vaPool for vector_artefacts writes, mainPool for read-only cross-DB owner decoration) — documented in lines 36–48 and called out in sql.go header. Reported as a warning, not a violation, because the cross-DB read is the documented escape hatch.
